approval_required_for: Any proposed architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, trusted-template, or numeric-policy change requires the applicable human approval before execution.

Any repair that would change checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy, tolerance, testbench contract, or exact board-wrapper source identity requires approval and must not be used to mask a DUT or integration defect.
No approval is evidenced as necessary for the audit-only action; human_boundary_check must determine permissions for any subsequent repair.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep SACG extraction blocked. Record each failing or unavailable checker, affected constraint, source evidence, and bounded repair or clarification owner. Preserve the prepared-input error until its actual content is classified. Do not alter golden/reference artifacts, loosen numeric policy, infer approval, or claim readiness from omitted details.
executable_actions.rationale: The visible summary does not contain the specialist findings, checker results, or the content of the single prepared-input error. Integrate the source audits and execute the registered static checks so readiness and each remaining gap are evidence-bound rather than inferred.

observations: The state summary lists the principal model, numeric, template, design-space, board, tool, and human-boundary input artifact classes. The compact candidate summary does not expose their detailed contents or the detailed specialist audit findings; this is a limitation of the supplied evidence, not proof that those artifacts do not exist.

prepared_inputs.errors contains one entry, but its content and classification are not supplied. It remains an unresolved blocker and must be tied to a source artifact and affected constraint before readiness can be assessed.
No registered checker outcomes are shown. Configured LLM policy and the existence of candidate artifacts do not establish that specialist reviews or static checks passed.
The current SACG memory truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. No historical memory record is treated as a current blocker.
The hierarchical learning context reports no validated lower-layer certificates. That is not, by itself, an input-preparation blocker or evidence of a hardware failure.

Verification planning must use current-source VCS compilation, elaboration, and linking as the acceptance standard. Simulation execution, runtime weight loading, golden comparisons, traces, output dumps, and numerical correctness are not additional acceptance prerequisites.

The DUT scope is Transformer blocks only. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail work must remain outside DUT implementation and DUT weight-coverage requirements.
proposed_actions: Collect the four specialist audit artifacts and detailed prepared-input error, run the registered cross-layer and boundary checkers, and produce the three required audit outputs plus an explicit error classification and constraint-to-evidence gap map.

Keep SACG extraction blocked until the prepared-input error is classified and all required checker outcomes are available and acceptable; route any confirmed defect to its bounded repair owner without silently rewriting specialist findings.
risks: Model identity, decoder configuration, shape bindings, and task scope cannot be cross-checked against the numeric policy or template bindings from the compact evidence shown.

Numeric precision, data order, transfer units, template coverage, and memory/runtime assumptions may conflict; the detailed audits and checker outcomes needed to confirm or rule out conflicts are not visible.
Board interface and deployment facts cannot be reconciled with source evidence or tool protocols from the supplied summary. Input readiness must not be represented as board or backend readiness.
The prepared-input error could concern a blocking source defect or a nonblocking issue; classifying it without its content would be unsupported.
Human approval and forbidden-action boundaries are not visible in detail. Do not infer approval permissions or authorize repairs until human_boundary_check and repair_boundary_check validate them.
No synthesis, implementation, deployment, or board-readiness claim is supported by this input-preparation evidence.

edges: Model configuration and task scope must agree with model shape and template coverage.
Numeric policy and parameter bindings must agree with the selected templates and model shapes.
Data order, transfer units, memory plans, runtime assumptions, and board interfaces must agree across their source evidence.
Design-space constraints must be compatible with the model, templates, board profile, and tool protocol.
Tool protocol and human-boundary rules constrain permitted verification, repair, and approval actions.
Prepared-input errors and specialist findings must be mapped to affected constraints before SACG extraction.

output.summary: The supplied summary identifies the relevant input classes, but does not expose the four specialist audit findings, checker results, or the content of the single prepared-input error. Cross-layer readiness for SACG extraction therefore cannot be established. Preserve the error and all unverified consistency questions as blockers; no synthesis, deployment, or board-readiness claim is supported.
